scope: real-title recipe metrics and actual Plurx immutable-VOD browser presentation

checks.c2_recipe_samples: Three tagged real SDR excerpts; three windows each; VBR plus CRF 18/23/28 on the current shipping encoder/scorer. Every candidate fails a quality or byte gate, so the baseline remains selected.
checks.bframes: Four actual immutable VOD outputs: two CC film excerpts times bf0/bf2. All raw video presentation slots are contiguous and unique from zero; bf2 uses signed version-1 CTO. Strict full decode passes and AAC packets have no timestamp gaps.
checks.chrome: Four outputs times cold mid-entry at 18 seconds, forward seek to 40 seconds, and backward seek to 8 seconds. All pass moving decoded-pixel hashes and monotonic RVFC presentation.
checks.safari: POST /session times out before any page or media is loaded. This is an automation environment failure, not a decoder verdict.
checks.vmaf: All 3,359 frames per recipe were scored against the matched CFR/scale source reference. B-frames show no consistent quality/byte benefit.

decisions.c2: Retain ordinary VBR on these three sources; do not change the default.
decisions.bframes: Retain the bf0 default and meaningful operator opt-in; do not claim compression graduation.

limits: The C2 driver exercises the production recipe projection and scoring policy, not the durable job/cache owner.
Private 60-second excerpts and 12-second holdouts do not guarantee whole-film quality.
Official CC sources omit color tags. Source-relative VOD comparison does not qualify C2 metadata or original mastering.
Chrome is an isolated headless HLS/MSE runtime, not a physical television.
Safari WebDriver is unavailable. Apple AVPlayer and Android Media3 have separately owned receipts.
No shipping-UI prepared handoff or audible HDMI acceptance is claimed by this receipt.
The first raw bf2 CTO is zero; FFprobe 9 adds one video tick to demuxed PTS. Retained raw-grid evidence distinguishes that interpretation from the authored timeline.
OS cache is uncontrolled and single capture timings are not throughput benchmarks.

cleanup.native_shared_public_assets: retained temporarily for parent-owned native probes, then delete

reproduction.browser_and_vod: Run from an independent repository clone. Copy capture-vod.cjs, probe-clients.mjs, inspect-served.py and score-vod.py into target/qualification/. Set PLURX_QUALIFICATION_SERVER to the pinned daemon, PLURX_HWACCEL=software and explicit PLURX_FFMPEG/PLURX_FFPROBE. The public-corpus URLs and hashes identify the inputs; copy-stream 60-second excerpts with input -ss 120 into public-clips/{animation,live-action}.mkv. capture-vod.cjs owns and removes the isolated daemon. The inspection/scoring scripts read its served/ outputs. Browser profiles and servers are temporary.
reproduction.private_content: Run qualify-content-encoding.py on the source node with a private manifest containing exactly three preselected source paths, anonymous identities, current source revision and three encoder-calibration-args exports for CRF 18/23/28 at 4000 kbps and two threads. The script creates one isolated current-image container with read-only source mounts, exports no media, emits numerical JSON, and removes its temporary media/container. The control manifest must remain private and be deleted afterward.
